text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi has announced that he will resign in the interests of a stable government as soon as a majority coalition can be formed in parliament. The premier discussed the political situation with his party leadership. The Coalition Party is recommending its vice-chairman, Mart Siimann, as the premier's candidate and he has been authorised to negotiate with parties.
- Legal experts have declared that the apartment deals conducted in central Tallinn were illegal. The deals were behind the no-confidence vote against Vaehi on Monday.
- Defence League chief Major Neeme Vali has offered to resign from the post following his conviction for negligence.

- Several hundred pupils demonstrated outside a provincial courthouse in defence of a grammar school director, who is charged with violence towards pupils, based on testimony of an alleged teenage hooligan. The case is to continue in late March.
- The western Viimsi local government decided to sell a land plot to President Lennart Meri
- Estonia will continue to claim back its cultural treasures from Russia, despite the law approved by the State Duma recently, which prevents their return.
- Estonian skier Kristiina Smigun came first at the junior world championship cross-country skiing in Canada.
- Moscow published a strategy document on relations with the Baltic states.
- The Rakvere meat-packing plant was the first in Estonia to receive a certificate allowing exports to European markets.
- Tolaram Group, a Singapore company, will make further investments in cellulose and paper production in Estonia.
